issues.problem: R11-02 is still incomplete: new variants of the same class pass the exact SKILL.md gate (verify --strict) with exit 0. (a) NUMBER_RE needs a word boundary after the digits, so compact figures are invisible: '$50M', '$7.5B' (reduced to '7'), '10k', 'FY2018', 'Q3', and product names with digits (EC2/S3, GPT4/GPT5); a thousands separator splits '2,500' into {'2','500'}, which '500 customers in 2 regions' satisfies. (b) _negation_conflict compares the claim with one quote clause chosen by raw token overlap, ties going to the first clause, so a quote that contradicts the claim in another clause or sentence still supports it ('Acme is SOC 2 certified' vs '... pursuing certification. It is not SOC 2 certified yet.'). (c) Only 30% of the claim's words must appear, so a figure re-attached to a different noun passes ('Acme had 500 employees in 2023' vs '... 12 offices and 500 customers'). Negation by prefix/word ('unsupported', 'absent', 'zero incidents') also passes. The documented limits (antonym/verb swaps, figure-free recommendations) cover none of (a)-(c), and the compute_support_score docstring says a supported claim 'contains every number'.

issues.suggested_fix: Extract numbers with their unit and scale and normalise them before comparing (e.g. r'(?<![\w.])[$€£]?\d{1,3}(?:,\d{3})+(?:\.\d+)?|\d+(?:\.\d+)?\s*(?:%|x|k|m|mn|bn|b|million|billion|thousand)?\b' -> 50e6, 7.5e9, 2500; treat FY/Q tokens and alphanumeric product ids such as EC2/GPT5 as entities). For negation, examine every quote clause that shares the claim's key terms (entities, numbers, rarest tokens) and flag a conflict if any of them disagrees, rather than one best clause with first-wins ties. Require each number to co-occur with the claim's nearest noun in the same quote clause, or raise MIN_TOKEN_OVERLAP for figure-bearing claims. Add these pairs as tests. If some of this is out of scope for v1, list each remaining class in quality-gates.md and mark R11-02 partial.

issues.problem: Regression in 197a8d6: _PinnedHTTPSConnection.connect replaces http.client's connect but never runs self._tunnel(), and it wraps TLS with server_hostname=self.host, the proxy host when a proxy is set. urllib's default ProxyHandler stays in the opener, so with HTTPS_PROXY set (common in corporate networks, and set in this environment) the verifier connects to the proxy and starts TLS directly instead of sending CONNECT. And when the proxy has a private or loopback address, _public_addresses rejects the proxy itself. Every DOI and https URL check then fails, so '<50% verified' fails the documented verify_citations command for every report behind a proxy unless --lenient is used. At 29714af the same calls used the CONNECT tunnel. No test covers proxies.
issues.evidence: REVF-H8a2-probe/bin/proxy_probe.py records what the client sends (socket.create_connection redirected to a local listener, every name resolving to a public address): 197a8d6 with HTTPS_PROXY=http://proxy.corp.example:3128 -> connect_to=[('93.184.216.34', 3128)], first bytes = TLS ClientHello (no CONNECT); 29714af -> connect_to=[('proxy.corp.example', 3128)], first bytes 'CONNECT'. bin/proxy2.py with the real resolver for IP-literal proxies: HTTPS_PROXY=http://10.20.30.40:3128 -> verify_doi (False, 'connection blocked (non-public address 10.20.30.40)'); http://127.0.0.1:9 -> same for 127.0.0.1.
issues.suggested_fix: In _PinnedHTTPSConnection/_PinnedHTTPConnection.connect, when self._tunnel_host is set: connect to the configured proxy without vetting it (the user's own proxy), call self._tunnel(), and wrap TLS with server_hostname=self._tunnel_host; vet the target through unsafe_url_reason as now. Alternatively, skip pinning when a proxy applies to the URL (urllib.request.getproxies / proxy_bypass). Add a test with HTTPS_PROXY set that asserts a CONNECT to the target host and SNI = target host.

issues.problem: Ctrl-C/SIGTERM handling is only half done. Live worker groups are killed, but the exception then leaves 'with ThreadPoolExecutor', whose __exit__ is shutdown(wait=True) without cancel_futures, so every queued worker still starts after the interrupt and runs to its timeout while the dispatcher hangs. With the defaults (max_agents 11, concurrency 6, timeout 600 s) one Ctrl-C can launch up to five new paid AI sessions and block for 10 minutes. An interrupt during the submit loop, outside the try, skips the cleanup entirely. Also no test checks that dispatch_phase_parallel installs the SIGTERM handler: replacing it with a no-op passes all 30 tests.
issues.evidence: REVF-H8a2-probe/bin/sigdrive.py (dispatcher under its own session, fake cursor recording START/TERM, timeout 25 s, concurrency 1, 3 items): SIGINT at +2.0 s -> first worker TERMed at +2.0 s, then 'START pid=14835' at +2.0 s and 'START pid=31651' at +27.1 s, each killed only by its own timeout; dispatcher exits after 51.9 s. Concurrency 2: third worker starts at +2.0 s after SIGTERM, dispatcher exits at 16.9 s. With concurrency 3 and 3 items all three are TERMed at +2.0 s and the dispatcher exits at 1.9 s. Sandbox revert 'restore = lambda: None' in dispatch_phase_parallel: test_worker_hardening 30 tests OK.
issues.suggested_fix: On BaseException in the dispatcher call pool.shutdown(wait=False, cancel_futures=True) (and/or set a module stop Event that _run_cli checks before Popen) before _terminate_live_workers(), and put the submit loop inside the try. Add a test with more items than concurrency asserting no launch after the interrupt, and a test that dispatch_phase_parallel turns SIGTERM into cleanup.

issues.problem: The claude worker does not run in permission mode 'default' as the docstring, the WORKER_PERMISSION_MODE comment and SKILL.md ('nothing auto-approved') claim. --use-print makes the delegate a pinned non-interactive launch (agent_delegate_exec_pinned_ni), and agent_host_build_argv maps --mode strict to '--permission-mode acceptEdits' and never reads CLAUDE_PERMISSION_MODE. The new _delegate_env pin therefore has no effect, and its test asserts only the wrapper's env, so it cannot see this, the same pattern as the previous round. Practical exposure is small (auto-accepted edits are confined to the empty throwaway cwd), but the stated guarantee is false.

issues.suggested_fix: Either launch claude directly like codex ('claude --print --permission-mode default --model ... --effort ...' with the prompt on stdin, cwd = sandbox), or document acceptEdits-in-an-empty-sandbox accurately and record the G6 need (agent-host-exec.sh:69 has no default/plan mapping for strict). Assert the final argv through a recording stub, not the wrapper env.
